Background:
BC Hydro is one of the largest electric utilities in Canada. We generate and provide electricity to 95  per  cent  of  British  Columbia's  population  and  serve  over  four  million  people.  The  system includes 35 hydroelectric facilities, 300 substations and over 79,000 kilometers of transmission and  distribution  lines  that  are  owned  and  operated  by  BC  Hydro.  In  addition,  BC  Hydro  has approximately 125 electricity  purchase agreements with independent power producers, which currently  make  up  about  25%  of  our  energy supply  on the  BC  Hydro  integrated  system.  The electricity generated and transmitted to our customers throughout the province has consistently powered B.C.'s economy and quality of life.
It  is  our mission to safely provide our customers with reliable, affordable, and clean electricity throughout B.C.

Strategic Objectives:
BC Hydro is taking a strategic approach to the management of the Call for Power to secure new energy resources for B.C.
Specifically, we plan to look at cost effective options to meet new demand, while also considering other objectives including:
- maintaining affordability of electricity;
- meeting  rising  customer  expectations  by  maintaining  a  reliable  power  system  that supports BC's growing economy;
- advancing reconciliation with First Nations; and
- reducing greenhouse gas emissions through clean and efficient electrification.

First Nations Economic Participation:
BC Hydro has worked in collaboration with First Nations on a First Nation economic participation model  to  ensure  that  this  RFP  creates  opportunities  for  meaningful  economic  benefits,  in alignment with our United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Implementation Plan, for First Nations. As noted in the plan, BC Hydro views calls for power as important opportunities for First Nations to advance self-determination and economic development  as  First  Nations  can  be  partners,  owners,  and  shareholders  in  Clean  Energy Projects. By entering such agreements, First Nations can get access to financial benefits and participate in decisions about how and when Projects proceed.
The First Nations economic participation model consists of three parts:
- a  mandatory  requirement  that  each  Proposal  meet  an  Eligibility  Requirement  of  a minimum 25% First Nations Equity Ownership in a Project;
- an optional evaluation credit to acknowledge First Nations Equity Ownership in excess of the minimum 25% First Nations Equity Ownership (up to 51%);
- an optional evaluation credit, the First Nations Community Economic Benefits Credit, for Proposals  that  provide  attestations  from  Proponents  and  First  Nations  which  indicate preliminary agreement is in place relating to community economic benefits.
The minimum First Nations Equity Ownership requirement will be assessed on a pass-fail basis. Proposals that fail to demonstrate the minimum 25% requirement will be disqualified.
Proposals that are in excess of the minimum 25% First Nations Equity Ownership and/or which provide attestations from Proponents and First Nations relating to community economic benefits may be eligible to receive Evaluation Price credit as further described in Section 11.2, Table 4, (C) & (D). These credits, as applicable, will have the effect of reducing the Evaluation Price for a Proposal,  effectively  making  the  Proposal  more  cost  effective  in  the  evaluation  process.  For greater certainty the Evaluation Price is solely for evaluation purposes and is not the amount paid for energy under an Electricity Purchase Agreement (EPA).

Canada Infrastructure Bank:
Prior to issuing this RFP, BC Hydro and the Canada Infrastructure Bank ( 'CIB' ) discussed the possibility of the CIB providing financing to support successful Proponents. The CIB has informed BC Hydro that, subject to its due diligence, the CIB will offer support to successful Proponents by providing an investment tax credit bridge loan (at the Project level) and a loan to finance First Nations equity participation (at the First Nations Equity Ownership level). It is anticipated that further information will be available to Proponents in late July 2025 directly from CIB. Draft credit documents will be available to Proponents who register interest at bchydro2025@cib-bic.ca.
While BC Hydro encourages Proponents to explore CIB funding opportunities, Proponents may seek  financing  for  their  Projects  from  any  financing  source  they  desire.  BC  Hydro  and  CIB maintain an arms-length relationship and Proponent questions about CIB financing should be addressed directly with CIB.

Each adjuster will be converted into a $/MWh value that is added or credited to the Proponent's levelized-real Bid Price to calculate the Evaluation Price in accordance with the following formula:
